title: Audit ingest stream governor, smart TTL tiers, and hotpath QoS
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an ingest-side stream governor and multi-tier TTL policy for audit logs to control cost and guarantee hotpath QoS. This ticket covers schema tagging at ingest (hot/warm/cold), adaptive partitioning, backpressure signals to producers, per-tenant cost thresholds, and an operator-facing emergency throttle. It also ties audit events for admin actions (RBAC v2 changes, SSO/SAML config events) to a higher-retention tier when marked high-sensitivity.
acceptance_criteria: A stream governor exists that can throttle or shed audit events by tenant and event type without dropping high-sensitivity admin events
Ingest pipeline tags each event with retention_tier: hot|warm|cold based on policy rules; tags are visible in index metadata
Index partitioning rotates by tenant+day for hot tier and by tenant+week for warm tier; cold tier is compacted and spilled to coldstore within TTL
Operator UI shows per-tenant ingress rate, estimated monthly cost, and current throttle status; we have an alert when a tenant will exceed configured budget in 24h
Migration plan defined for retroactively reclassifying existing indices and a safe backfill path with minimal cluster impact
Performance tests demonstrate <=15ms median write-latency for hot tier under 5k rps baseline and graceful degradation under overload
All changes covered by unit/integration tests and a staging canary run with simulated tenant spikes

implementation_notes: Ingest pipeline: add 'retention_tier' and 'sensitivity' fields at the first producer boundary to avoid downstream reclassification costs
Governor uses per-tenant token buckets + priority lanes: admin_high (immutable admin events), default, bulk_low (telemetry)
Partitioning: hot indices rolled hourly for high-volume tenants; warm rolled daily with segment compaction weekly; cold tier writes use append-only blobs with index summaries
Cost controls: per-tenant spend estimate computed from historical token counts x cost-per-token, exposed via billing-estimator API
Backpressure signals: implement HTTP 429 with Retry-After when shedding to let producers back off; provide client SDKs with optional local buffering
RBAC v2: changes to roles/permissions must include an 'audit_sensitivity' annotation during write to ensure classification; migration helpers in security-api to populate missing annotations
SSO/SAML: configuration change events flagged as high-sensitivity and routed to immutable hot lane; retention set per policy (default 365d), configurable by security admins
Fallback: if cluster load threatens SLOs, non-sensitive events are sampled deterministically using tenant-aware reservoir sampling instead of dropping uniformly
Observability: add histograms for per-tenant ingest latency, per-tier storage growth, and a daily job that validates retention enforcement (and reports drift)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Misclassification of events could cause loss of forensic data. Mitigation: keep a 72h write-through buffer for all events that allows reclassification and backfill into hot tier if a classification bug is discovered

Risk: Throttling could cause upstream producer errors and customer-visible failures. Mitigation: provide client SDKs and webhooks for backpressure, plus a tenant-level fail-open emergency toggle for trusted enterprise customers

Risk: Cost savings vs. query latency trade-off for cold tier. Mitigation: support auto-promote of cold blobs to warm on detection of query patterns and maintain coldstore index summaries for quick filter pruning
testing_plan: Unit tests for tagging rules and token-bucket behavior
Integration: staging canary with 10 synthetic tenants including one high-volume tenant simulating 10k rps
Load tests: baseline and overload targets; verify hot-tier <=15ms median write-latency at 5k rps
Chaos test: simulate coldstore unavailability and validate failover to limited warm retention
Security review: confirm admin action immutability and verify SSO/SAML event flags cannot be downgraded by non-admins
rollout_plan: Week 1: Deploy governor and tagging to staging; run canary workload
Week 2: Small production pilot with 5 willing tenants; monitor costs and SLOs
Week 3: Gradual rollout to 50% of write volume with automatic rollback if per-tenant latency SLO violated
Week 4: Full rollout and enable billing-estimator alerts and operator emergency throttle in Console
